headline: Coal from Kazakhstan is becoming more expensive by the time it reaches Uzbekistan; heating companies complain about transport costs
summary: Shubarkol coal from Kazakhstan costs $40 a tonne at the Uzbek border but reaches greenhouses at up to $110, businesses say, citing rail transport, unloading and intermediaries.
why: Coal is an energy input for greenhouses and industry, so delivered price increases raise operating costs for heating-dependent producers.
